title: Flat-term K-flat complexes are closed under short exact extensions
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and 0 -> A -> B -> C -> 0 a short exact sequence of integer cochain complexes of R-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume every term of A and C is flat, and A and C are K-flat for the signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Then every term of B is flat and B is K-flat. The sequence need not split in any degree, and the complexes need not be bounded.

source.place: Lemma lemma-K-flat-two-out-of-three-ses, proof (tensor the short exact sequence and use homology); flatness of the middle terms is literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex, Lemma lemma-flat-ses.

proof.text: For a short exact module sequence with flat quotient, the module tensor row is short exact by flat quotient tensor injectivity and right exactness. Tensor the row with a monomorphism N->N' and use the short five lemma (mono version) with the two flat outer terms to prove flatness of the middle module.

For any complex E, tensor the complex short exact sequence with E. Right exactness of total tensor supplies exactness and epimorphy. In degree n, its first map is induced between coproducts indexed by (p,q) with p+q=n; each summand map is monic by flat quotient tensor injectivity. Exact coproducts of modules make the total map monic. Hence the tensor sequence is short exact.

Use the homotopy-category criterion for K-flatness: tensoring with any acyclic complex is acyclic. The first and third terms of the tensor sequence are acyclic by K-flatness. Exactness of its homology sequence makes the middle term acyclic. The signed braiding gives the other tensor side. Apply the module flat-extension conclusion in each degree.
